Letter Drop

0
points no words yet

    How to play

    You start with a five-letter word. Each round you keep some of its letters and add one more, making a word one letter shorter, until you are down to a single letter.

    1. 5 → 4 Keep three letters in a row, add one.
    2. 4 → 3 Keep two letters in a row, add one.
    3. 3 → 2 Keep one letter, add one.
    4. 2 → 1 If your two-letter word holds an A or an I, it falls on its own. Those are the only one-letter words.

    Two rules

    • The letters you keep stay side by side and in order, so the letter you add goes on one end, never in the middle.
    • Every letter you add must be one you have not used yet. Anything already on the board, the opening word included, is greyed out on the keyboard.

    Taking a turn

    Tap letters to keep them and they drop as soon as you have enough. Type a letter, tap the empty slot at either end to choose which end it lands on, then tap the green check. Words come from a Scrabble dictionary, so a few odd ones are legal.

    Scoring

    • 2 points for every word you make.
    • 1, 2 or 3 points for the letter it brings in, depending on how awkward that letter is to use. The small number in the corner of each key says which, the way a Scrabble tile does. The last letter falls without adding one, so that round is worth 2.
    • 3 points for getting all the way down to a single letter. Stop short and you lose them, so the expensive letter is not always worth taking.
    • Undo costs 1 point once there is a word to take back. Backing out of a split you have not committed is free, and your score never goes below zero.

    Every deal has its own best possible score, shown beside your running total from the start. Reaching it means going after the awkward letters rather than the easy ones. A bad split can also leave you with nothing to make at all, and then only Undo will save you.

    Hints

    Turn Hints on and every letter that makes a word from where you stand gets a green ring. It is there to learn with, so a run played with hints on counts as practice and cannot be shared.
